digest.component_or_area: reconciler rich-text send path cutover + echo suppression + conflict safety
propositions: Cloud and DC send paths must convert to rich codecs (ADF markdown-aware on Cloud, rendered wiki on DC) without re-posting already-synced bodies across consecutive passes.

Echo suppression is state-based (current Jira value vs. last-synced baseline), not codec-identity based, with an 8-byte inline change-gated rich_sha counter reset only when the wire differs, triggering one GET-and-overlay at exactly 2 consecutive identical renders.

DC's WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound must be redefined to decode(to_wire(t)) to restore the codec law, and both DC create paths must compose to_wire(fit_outbound(value)), or newly created issues ship raw Markdown while updates ship rendered wiki.

Two distinct compare operations coexist: emit compares normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local)) vs decode_inbound(remote_wire) to cancel lossy round-trip; baseline compares local through normalize_outbound vs decode(baseline_wire), so unchanged Jira-authored constructs survive edit-free passes and rebar edits show changed.

The cutover must degrade to plain-text ADF behaviour (today's path) without error when marklas is absent or the feature flag is OFF, and concurrent both-sides body edits route to the outbound-field-conflict alert with local-wins semantics unchanged.

A rebar-originated change (local != baseline) fires outbound; baseline advances only via _advance_baselines, never the post-push GET; benign re-canonicalization converges in one re-emit with no re-GET, and the inline state adds ≤0.07 KB/version with zero entries changed on no-op passes.
